subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Ford vs Ferrari at Le Mans
description: A 60-second lesson on Ford vs Ferrari at Le Mans.

hook.text: In 1963, Henry Ford II tried to buy Ferrari. Enzo Ferrari said no—and insulted him publicly.

buildup.text: Ford poured millions into building the GT40—a car designed to beat Ferrari at Le Mans.

discovery.text: After embarrassing failures in 1964 and 1965, Ford hired Carroll Shelby to fix the car.

twist.text: In 1966, Ford finished first, second, and third—crushing Ferrari's decade of Le Mans dominance.

climax.text: The GT40 won Le Mans four years in a row, making it the most dominant car in endurance history.

punchline.text: Ford built a Le Mans legend entirely out of spite.

quiz.question: Why did Ford build the GT40?
options: To beat Ferrari at Le Mans after a failed buyout

details.summary: Ford's quest to defeat Ferrari at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the 1960s produced the GT40, which won four consecutive Le Mans victories from 1966 to 1969 in one of motorsport's greatest rivalries.
details.whyItMatters: The Ford-Ferrari war showed how corporate rivalry can drive extraordinary engineering. Ford's victory proved that American ingenuity and resources could beat European racing aristocracy.
takeaways: Henry Ford II funded the GT40 program after Ferrari rejected his buyout
The GT40 won Le Mans four consecutive years from 1966 to 1969
The 1966 finish saw three GT40s cross the line in formation

faq.question: Why did Ford want to buy Ferrari?
faq.answer: Ford wanted Ferrari's racing prestige and European cachet. When Enzo Ferrari backed out of the deal at the last minute over control of racing operations, Henry Ford II vowed to beat Ferrari on the track instead.

faq.question: Is the story accurately told in the 2019 movie?
faq.answer: The film captures the spirit of the rivalry accurately but takes dramatic liberties with timelines and character details. The core engineering achievement and personal dramas are well represented.
